title.zh: 卷一百八十九 志第一百四十二 兵三
title.raw: 卷一百八十九 志第一百四十二 兵三 Volume 189 Treatises 142: Military 3

translations.literal: Corridor troops are the garrison troops of the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Corridor troops were the garrison forces stationed in the prefectures.

translations.literal: In the capital they were placed under the overall authority of the Palace Command.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, they fell under the overall jurisdiction of the Palace Command.

sentences.zh: 一軍之額，有分隸數州者，或一州之管兼屯數州者，在京諸司之額五，隸宣徽院，以分給畜牧繕修之役，而諸州則各以其事屬焉。

translations.literal: For the quota of a single army, some were subordinated across several prefectures, or a single prefecture's jurisdiction might garrison several prefectures together; in the capital there were five quotas for the various offices, subordinate to the Court of the Palace Attendants, to assign them to duties of herding livestock and repair work, while in the prefectures each attached them to its own affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A single army's authorized strength might be divided among several prefectures, or one prefecture might oversee garrisons spanning several prefectures. In the capital, five authorized quotas for the various offices were subordinate to the Court of the Palace Attendants and assigned to herding, repair, and similar duties; in the prefectures, each jurisdiction attached corridor troops to its own tasks.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，選諸州募兵之壯勇者部送京師，以備禁衛，餘留本城，雖無戍更，然罕教閱，類多給役而已。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong, the stout and brave among recruited troops from the various prefectures were selected and escorted to the capital to serve as palace guards; the remainder were left in their home garrisons. Although they had no rotation for frontier duty, they were rarely drilled and for the most part were only assigned to labor service.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianlong reign, the strongest recruits from the prefectures were selected and sent to the capital for the palace guard; the rest remained in local garrison. They did not rotate to frontier posts, were seldom drilled, and were largely used only as labor detachments.

sentences.zh: 景德四年七月，如京使何士宗言：「詔條禁軍將士依等級並行伏事之理，違者按軍令。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Jingde, He Shizong, Commissioner on Assignment to the Capital, said: "The edict articles for palace-guard officers and soldiers require them to observe the principle of performing menial service according to rank; violators are to be punished under military law.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Jingde 4 (1007), He Shizong, commissioner on assignment to the capital, reported: "The edict stipulates that palace-guard officers and soldiers must perform menial duties according to rank, with violators punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 其廂軍將士等未立條制，欲望約前詔減一等定令。」

translations.literal: For corridor-troop officers and soldiers no regulations have yet been established; it is desired to draw on the previous edict and reduce the grade by one level in fixing the rules."
translations.idiomatic: Corridor-troop officers and soldiers have no comparable regulations yet. I request that we adapt the earlier edict, reducing penalties by one grade."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「禁衛兵士無他役使，且廩給優厚，欲其整肅，有所凜畏，故設此條禁。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Palace-guard soldiers have no other assignments, and their rations and pay are generous; we wish them to be disciplined and to have something to fear, and therefore established these prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Palace guards have no other duties, and their pay and rations are generous. We want them disciplined and mindful of authority, which is why these strict rules were set.

sentences.zh: 今以廂軍約此施行，恐難經久。

translations.literal: To apply this now to corridor troops by analogy, I fear it will be hard to maintain for long.
translations.idiomatic: Applying the same rules to corridor troops would probably not last.

sentences.zh: 況尊卑相犯，自有條律，不行可也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, when superiors and inferiors offend one another, there are already statutes; it need not be implemented."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, offenses between ranks of superior and inferior are already covered by statute. We need not put this into effect."

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔廂軍及諸州本城犯，所部決杖訖，並移隸他軍，內情理重及緣邊隨軍者奏裁。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict ordered that when corridor troops and local-garrison troops of the various prefectures committed offenses, after beating with the staff was decided in their unit, they were all to be transferred to other armies; cases of grave circumstances and those on campaign along the frontier were to be reported for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, an edict ruled that corridor troops and local garrison troops who offended were, after corporal punishment in their unit, to be transferred to another command. Grave cases and soldiers on frontier campaign were to be reported to the throne for decision.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，詔應諸道州、府、軍、監廂軍及本城指揮，自都指揮使已下至長行，對本轄人員有犯階級者，並於禁軍斬罪上減等，從流三千里上定斷；

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict ordered that for corridor troops and local-garrison commands in all circuits, prefectures, armies, and supervisory posts, from the commander-in-chief down to the common soldier, when they offended against rank within their jurisdiction, all were to have their penalties reduced one grade from the capital-guard standard for offenses warranting decapitation, with final judgment fixed at exile for three thousand li or more;
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 1 (1008), an edict directed that in every circuit, prefecture, army, and supervisory post, corridor and local-garrison commands—from the commander-in-chief down to the rank-and-file—who offended against rank within their unit would have penalties reduced one grade below the palace-guard capital punishment standard, with final sentencing at exile of three thousand li or more;

sentences.zh: 副兵馬使已上，勘罪具案聞奏。

translations.literal: for deputy horse-and-foot commissioners and above, the crime was to be investigated, the case fully prepared, and reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: for deputy horse-and-foot commissioners and above, offenses were to be investigated, fully documented, and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 廂軍軍頭已下至長行，准敕犯流免配役，並徒三年上定斷，只委逐處決訖，節級已上配別指揮長行上名，長行決訖，配別指揮下名收管。

translations.literal: For corridor-troop squad leaders down to common soldiers, in accordance with the edict, offenses of exile exempted corvée assignment, and all were fixed at penal servitude of three years or more; authority was delegated to each locality to decide and conclude; those of company grade and above were assigned to the upper rolls of another command, and after common soldiers were decided, they were assigned to the lower rolls of another command for custody.
translations.idiomatic: For corridor-troop squad leaders down to rank-and-file, per the edict, exile offenses exempted corvée, with sentences fixed at three years' penal servitude or more. Local authorities were to decide cases. Company-grade offenders and above were transferred to the upper rolls of another command; rank-and-file, once sentenced, went to the lower rolls of another command.

sentences.zh: 如本處別無軍分指揮，即配鄰近州、府、軍、監指揮收管。

translations.literal: If locally there was no other army-branch command, they were to be assigned to a neighboring prefecture, army, or supervisory command for custody.
translations.idiomatic: If no other command existed locally, offenders were assigned to a neighboring prefecture, army, or supervisory post.

translations.literal: Among them, those with separate grave offenses were to be punished under the heavier law.
translations.idiomatic: Separate grave offenses were punished under the heavier statute.

sentences.zh: 其諸司庫務人員兵士有犯上件罪名者，並依前項廂軍條例施行。

translations.literal: Personnel and soldiers of the various offices and storehouses who committed the above-listed offenses were all to be handled according to the preceding corridor-troop regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel and soldiers of government offices and storehouses who committed the listed offenses were subject to the same corridor-troop rules.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，上諭王欽若等：「累議老病之兵漸多，在京者令逐司將臣，外處者散差諸司使副揀選。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, the Emperor instructed Wang Qinruo and others: "It has been repeatedly discussed that old and sick soldiers are gradually increasing. For those in the capital, order the generals of each office; for those outside, dispatch envoys and vice-envoys of the various offices to make selections.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 5, the emperor told Wang Qinruo and others: "We have repeatedly discussed the growing number of old and sick soldiers. In the capital, each office's generals should handle selection; outside the capital, envoys and deputies from the various offices should be dispatched to screen them.

sentences.zh: 可指揮所揀殿前、侍衛馬步軍司，令先逐指揮自指揮使已下，據見管兵士除堪任披帶征役外，其自來懦弱、教閱不出之人及老病不堪者，籍其名，供申次第，管轄處各就逐營看詳定奪，然後繳申逐司，與差去使臣同共揀選。

translations.literal: You may order the selected commands of the Palace Front and Palace Horse-and-Foot Commands to have each command, from the commander down, based on the soldiers currently under their charge, apart from those fit to bear arms on campaign, register by name those who have always been weak, who fail to appear at drill, and who are old or sick and unfit, report them in sequence, have each jurisdiction examine and decide at each camp, then submit the lists to each office and conduct selection together with the dispatched envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Order the Palace Front and Palace Horse-and-Foot Commands to have each command, from the commander down, list every soldier under their charge who is unfit for active campaign—those habitually weak, absent from drill, or old and sick—while keeping those fit for field service. Each jurisdiction should review its camps, decide cases, submit rosters to the responsible office, and conduct joint screening with the dispatched envoys.

sentences.zh: 如有協情不當，即具始末以聞。

translations.literal: If there is collusion or improper favoritism, report the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Report the full circumstances of any collusion or improper favoritism.

sentences.zh: 其廂軍都指揮使已下並當嚴斷，外處揀就糧兵士亦如之。」

translations.literal: For corridor troops, commanders-in-chief and below are all to be strictly punished; the same applies to grain-paid soldiers selected outside the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Corridor-troop commanders-in-chief and subordinates who fail in this duty are to be strictly punished; the same applies to grain-paid soldiers screened in the provinces."

sentences.zh: 又宣示：「外處就糧諸軍，有捧日、天武第七第九第十軍軍額，皆是自上軍經兩三度揀選，以其久處禁衛，不欲便揀落，特設上件軍額處之。

translations.literal: He further announced: "Among grain-paid armies outside the capital, the designations of the Sun-Upholding, Heavenly Martial Seventh, Ninth, and Tenth Armies were all drawn from top-grade units after two or three rounds of selection; because they had long served in the palace guard and we did not wish to demote them at once, these army designations were specially established to place them.
translations.idiomatic: He further announced: "Among provincial grain-paid units, the Sun-Upholding and Heavenly Martial Seventh, Ninth, and Tenth Armies were formed from top-grade troops after two or three screenings. Because they had long served in the palace guard, we did not wish to demote them immediately and created these designations for them.

sentences.zh: 朕深慮揀兵臣僚、軍頭等同諸軍例，更揀配下軍，可遍諭之。

translations.literal: I deeply fear that the officials and squad leaders selecting troops will treat them like other armies and reassign them to lower armies; this should be announced everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: I am concerned that screening officials and squad leaders will treat them like other units and reassign them to lower commands. Make this known everywhere.

sentences.zh: 老病者便放歸農，內契丹、渤海、日本外國人恐無依倚，特與收充本軍剩員。」

translations.literal: The old and sick may be released to return to farming; among them, Khitan, Bohai, and Japanese foreigners, fearing they would have no support, are specially allowed to be retained as surplus personnel of their original army.
translations.idiomatic: Release the old and sick to farming. Khitan, Bohai, and Japanese foreigners, who might have nowhere to go, may be retained as surplus rolls in their original commands.

sentences.zh: 又：「所差臣僚、軍頭赴外處揀人。

translations.literal: Further: "The dispatched officials and squad leaders go outside to select men.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Dispatched officials and squad leaders will go to the provinces to screen troops.

sentences.zh: 緣軍分指揮及出入次第名目體例甚多，令樞密院具合行條約及施行事件，並畫一處分，令遵守施行。」

translations.literal: Because army branches, commands, and the many titles, sequences, and protocols for movement are numerous, order the Bureau of Military Affairs to prepare the applicable regulations and implementing matters, draw up uniform disposition, and have them obeyed and carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Because army branches, commands, and the many rules for titles, sequence, and transfers are complex, the Bureau of Military Affairs shall prepare applicable regulations and procedures, set uniform rules, and ensure they are followed."

sentences.zh: 又：「殿前、侍衛馬步軍司自來揀下披帶禁軍，量減衣賜月糧充剩員，並無定額，散在逐營拘系，不獲營生，官中所給歲計不少，可乘此時一例揀選。

translations.literal: Further: "The Palace Front and Palace Horse-and-Foot Commands have always selected down palace guards fit to bear arms, reduced their clothing allowance and monthly grain to serve as surplus personnel, with no fixed quota, scattered in each camp under restraint, unable to make a living; what the government gives yearly is not small—this opportunity may be used for a general selection.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The palace commands have long demoted armed guards to surplus rolls with reduced pay, with no fixed quota, scattered in camps and unable to earn a living, yet costing the treasury heavily each year. Use this screening to consolidate them.

sentences.zh: 除老病者放歸農外，據諸軍見管人數額定充看營剩員，餘並撥並一處收管，以備令赴諸處祗應。

translations.literal: Apart from releasing the old and sick to farming, fix surplus camp-watch personnel according to each army's current head count, consolidate the remainder in one place for custody, and prepare them to be sent on assignment to various places.
translations.idiomatic: Release the old and sick to farming. Fix camp-watch surplus rolls according to each army's authorized strength. Consolidate the rest in one pool for dispatch on assignment.

sentences.zh: 既有定額，必不敢多揀充剩員。」

translations.literal: Once there is a fixed quota, they will certainly not dare to select many as surplus personnel.
translations.idiomatic: With fixed quotas, commanders will not dare to inflate surplus rolls.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「承前遣使取內外軍中疲老者，咸給奉糧之半，以隸剩員，今可簡閱使歸農。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered: "Previously envoys were sent to take the worn-out and old from armies inside and outside; all were given half pay and attached as surplus personnel. Now they may be reviewed and sent back to farming.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered: "Previously, envoys collected worn-out soldiers from all armies, paid them half rations as surplus personnel. Now review them and release them to farming.

sentences.zh: 其合留者，亦據逐營給役數外別爲營舍處之。

translations.literal: Those who should remain are also, beyond the labor quota of each camp, to be housed separately in barracks.
translations.idiomatic: Those retained beyond each camp's labor quota shall be housed in separate barracks.

sentences.zh: 內契丹、渤海、日本外國人慮無所歸，且依舊。

translations.literal: Among them, Khitan, Bohai, and Japanese foreigners, fearing they would have nowhere to go, are for the present to remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan, Bohai, and Japanese foreigners, who might have nowhere to go, may remain as before for now.

sentences.zh: 仍令所至州郡並與總管、鈐轄閱驗，連書其狀，具當去留之數，及引視軍校之不任職者，附驛以聞。

translations.literal: They are also to have each prefecture and commandery reached, together with the overall commander and the military controller, review and verify, jointly write up their condition, specify the numbers to go or stay, and present for inspection military officers unfit for duty, reporting by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: At each prefecture, overall commanders and military controllers shall jointly verify records, state how many are to go or stay, present unfit officers for inspection, and report by express post.

sentences.zh: 其當從隸軍額，即就配近便州郡；

translations.literal: Those who should follow army quotas are to be assigned on the spot to convenient nearby prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Those to remain in military rolls are assigned to convenient nearby prefectures;

sentences.zh: 緣邊者徙於內地，並與本州官吏移牒轉送；

translations.literal: those on the frontier are to be moved to the interior, and officials of the home prefecture are to transfer them by official correspondence;
translations.idiomatic: frontier troops are moved inland, with home-prefecture officials transferring them by official correspondence;

sentences.zh: 當停者給與公驗，止許居本州，歲申上其籍，並給次月奉糧、裝錢、日食遣之。

translations.literal: those to be discharged are given public credentials, permitted to reside only in their home prefecture, report their registers yearly, and are given the next month's pay, travel money, and daily provisions for their departure.
translations.idiomatic: those discharged receive public credentials, may reside only in their home prefecture, report yearly, and receive one month's pay, travel allowance, and daily rations for the journey.

sentences.zh: 所簡馬，但筋齒弱、老病不療者，件析以聞。

translations.literal: For horses screened out, only those with weak sinews and teeth or old and sick beyond cure are to be itemized and reported.
translations.idiomatic: List and report only horses with weak sinews and teeth or incurable old age and sickness.

sentences.zh: 在京殿前、馬步軍司有所升退，即時具名籍申樞密院，未當者悉改正之；

translations.literal: In the capital, when the Palace Front and Horse-and-Foot Commands have promotions or demotions, they are immediately to submit name registers to the Bureau of Military Affairs; what is improper is all to be corrected;
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, the palace commands shall immediately report promotions and demotions to the Bureau of Military Affairs and correct any improprieties;

sentences.zh: 當徙者給裝錢，在道只給糧；

translations.literal: those to be transferred are given travel money; on the road they receive only grain;
translations.idiomatic: transferees receive travel money and grain only while en route;

sentences.zh: 當停者給一月奉糧，勿復奏裁。

translations.literal: those to be discharged are given one month's pay, without further memorial for decision.
translations.idiomatic: discharges receive one month's pay without further memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 外州軍士當降以次軍分者，所隸州郡聽自擇。」

translations.literal: For soldiers outside the capital who should be demoted to the next lower army branch, the prefecture to which they are attached may allow them to choose."
translations.idiomatic: Provincial soldiers demoted to a lower army branch may choose their assigned prefecture."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「廣南東西、荊湖南北、福建、江南、京西等七路諸州、府、軍、監見管雜犯配隸軍人等，各差使臣一人，馳驛往逐處與轉運使、副或提點臣僚、知州、通判、鈐轄、都監、監押同共簡選，就近體量人數，分配側近州軍本城收管。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered: "In the seven circuits of Guangnan East and West, Jinghu South and North, Fujian, Jiangnan, and Jingxi, for miscellaneous offenders assigned to military service now under the various prefectures, armies, and supervisory posts, dispatch one envoy each by post relay to each place to conduct joint selection with the transport commissioner or deputy, the investigating official, the prefect, the vice-prefect, the military controller, the overall supervisor, or the jail warden, estimate numbers nearby, and assign them to local-garrison custody in neighboring prefectures and armies.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered envoys to the seven circuits of Guangnan, Jinghu, Fujian, Jiangnan, and Jingxi to join transport commissioners, investigating officials, prefects, vice-prefects, military controllers, and supervisors in screening miscellaneous offenders assigned to military service, estimate numbers locally, and assign them to nearby local garrisons.

sentences.zh: 如年老病患，委實久遠不任醫治充役者，放令逐便；

translations.literal: If old or sick and truly unable for a long time to be cured or serve, release them as they wish;
translations.idiomatic: release the old and sick who are beyond cure or service;

sentences.zh: 其少壯者即差人管押赴闕引見，當議選配近上軍分。

translations.literal: the young and strong are to be escorted to court for audience, and higher army branches are to be considered for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: escort the able-bodied to court for audience and consider assigning them to higher commands.

sentences.zh: 如不願量移及赴闕者，亦聽其便，仍於軍分量與遷改。

translations.literal: If they do not wish transfer or going to court, their convenience is also allowed, and they are still given promotion or change within the army.
translations.idiomatic: those unwilling to transfer or go to court may stay, with promotion or reassignment within their command.

sentences.zh: 如地遠勾抽遲延，即馳驛分路簡訖，具析以聞。」

translations.literal: If distant places delay summons, then by post relay complete selection by separate routes and report itemized details."
translations.idiomatic: if distant places delay, complete screening by separate express routes and report in detail."

sentences.zh: 七年，詔：「今後軍回在京者且未編排，依例引見。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict ordered: "Henceforth armies returning to the capital are not yet to be arranged; audience is to follow precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7, an edict ruled that returning armies in the capital were not to be reorganized immediately but presented for audience as usual.

sentences.zh: 內有老疾合配外處軍分，及看倉庫、草場神衛剩員並看營剩員等，與限歇泊半月後，編排引見訖，限五日般移。

translations.literal: Among them, the old and sick fit for assignment to outside army branches, and surplus Divine Guard warehouse-watchers, fodder-field watchers, and camp watchers, are to be given a limit of half a month to rest in quarters; after arrangement and audience are concluded, relocation is limited to five days.
translations.idiomatic: The old and sick fit for provincial assignment, surplus Divine Guard warehouse and fodder-field watchers, and camp watchers were allowed half a month to rest, then after audience had five days to relocate.

sentences.zh: 其外處軍回經過兵士並依此例，仍見訖與假十日，令移隸所配處。」

translations.literal: Soldiers of armies returning from outside who pass through are also to follow this precedent; after audience they are given ten days' leave to transfer to their assigned place."
translations.idiomatic: Provincial troops passing through on return followed the same rule, with ten days' leave after audience to reach their assignment."

sentences.zh: 八年，詔：「諸路轉運司、殿前侍衛馬步軍軍頭司、三司、宣徽院、開封府、諸司庫務等處人員兵士等，如內有殺賊得功及諸般使喚得力者，或因官中取索之時具詣實結罪供，申所轄去處，保明申奏。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict ordered: "For personnel and soldiers of the various circuit transport offices, the Palace Front and Palace Horse-and-Foot squad offices, the State Finance Commission, the Court of the Palace Attendants, Kaifeng Prefecture, and the various office storehouses, if among them are those who killed bandits with merit or proved capable in various assignments, when the government requisitions them they are to submit sworn truthful statements under penalty, report to their jurisdiction, obtain certification, and memorialize."
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, an edict directed transport offices, palace squad offices, the State Finance Commission, the Court of the Palace Attendants, Kaifeng Prefecture, and office storehouses: when requisitioning personnel or soldiers who had killed bandits with merit or proved capable in service, submit sworn truthful statements, obtain certification from their jurisdiction, and memorialize the throne."

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，詔選天下廂兵遷隸禁軍者凡五千餘人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi, an edict selected corridor troops from all under Heaven to be transferred to the palace guard, more than five thousand men in all.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi 1 (1017), an edict transferred more than five thousand corridor troops nationwide into the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔：「河北禁軍疲老不任力役者，委本路提點刑獄臣僚簡閱，不得庇匿，以費廩糧。」

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered: "For worn-out and old palace guards in Hebei unfit for labor service, commission the circuit's investigating censor to review them; sheltering or concealing them is forbidden, lest granary grain be wasted."
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, an edict ordered the Hebei investigating censor to screen worn-out palace guards unfit for labor, forbidding concealment that wasted state grain."

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，招收廣南巡海水軍、忠敢、澄海，雖曰廂軍，皆予旗鼓訓練，備戰守之役。

translations.literal: During Qingli, the Guangnan patrol naval forces, Loyal Bold, and Clear Sea were recruited; although called corridor troops, all were given banners and drums for training to prepare for combat and garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era, the Guangnan patrol navy and the Loyal Bold and Clear Sea units were recruited. Though classified as corridor troops, they received banners and drums, were drilled, and served in defense.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，河北水災，農民流入京東三十余萬，安撫使富弼募以爲兵，拔其尤壯者得九指揮，教以武技。

translations.literal: During Huangyou, floods in Hebei drove more than three hundred thousand peasants into Jingdong; the pacification commissioner Fu Bi recruited them as soldiers, selecting the stoutest into nine commands and teaching them martial skills.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou, Hebei floods drove more than three hundred thousand peasants into Jingdong. Pacification Commissioner Fu Bi recruited them as soldiers, forming nine commands from the strongest and training them in arms.

sentences.zh: 雖廩以廂兵，而得禁兵之用，且無驕橫難制之患。

translations.literal: Although maintained as corridor troops, they obtained the use of palace guards yet without the trouble of arrogance and difficulty of control.
translations.idiomatic: Though paid as corridor troops, they served like palace guards without the arrogance and unruliness of the capital army.

sentences.zh: 詔以其騎兵爲教閱騎射、威邊，步兵爲教閱壯武、威勇，分置青、萊、淄、徐、沂、密、淮陽七州軍，征役同禁軍。

translations.literal: An edict made their cavalry the Drilled Cavalry Archers and Border Guard, their infantry the Drilled Strong Martial and Martial Valor, placed in seven prefectures and armies—Qing, Lai, Zi, Xu, Yi, Mi, and Huaiyang—with campaign service the same as palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named their cavalry the Drilled Cavalry Archers and Border Guard and their infantry the Drilled Strong Martial and Martial Valor, stationing them in Qing, Lai, Zi, Xu, Yi, Mi, and Huaiyang, with campaign duties equal to palace guards.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐四年，復詔西路於鄆、濮、齊、兗、濟、單州置步兵指揮六，如東路法。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiayou, an edict again ordered six infantry commands established on the western route in Yan, Pu, Qi, Yan, Ji, and Shan prefectures, following the eastern-route method.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 4 (1059), an edict established six infantry commands on the western route in Yan, Pu, Qi, Yan, Ji, and Shan, following the eastern-route model.

sentences.zh: 於是東南州軍多置教閱廂軍，皆以威勇、忠果、壯武爲號，訓肄如禁軍、免其他役。

translations.literal: Thereupon many southeastern prefectures and armies established drilled corridor troops, all taking designations such as Martial Valor, Loyal Fruit, and Strong Martial, trained and disciplined like palace guards and exempt from other service.
translations.idiomatic: Many southeastern prefectures then formed drilled corridor commands named Martial Valor, Loyal Fruit, Strong Martial, and the like, trained like palace guards and exempt from other labor.

sentences.zh: 治平初，遣使分募河北、河東、陝西、京東民爲本城，遇就糧禁軍闕，即遣補。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhiping, envoys were sent to recruit separately among the people of Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, and Jingdong as local garrison; when vacancies occurred in grain-paid palace guards, they were immediately sent to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhiping, envoys recruited local garrison troops in Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, and Jingdong and filled grain-paid palace-guard vacancies as they arose.

sentences.zh: 又陝西州軍悉置壯城如河北，以備繕完城壘之役。

translations.literal: Shaanxi prefectures and armies also all established Strong City units as in Hebei, to prepare for repairing and completing walls and ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi prefectures also established Strong City units like Hebei for repairing walls and fortifications.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，本城四十三萬八千，逮治平三年，乃五十萬。

translations.literal: In Jingyou, local garrison numbered four hundred thirty-eight thousand; by the third year of Zhiping it reached five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Local garrison numbered 438,000 in Jingyou; by Zhiping 3 (1066) it had reached 500,000.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年五月，詔以禁軍分五部法檢治廂軍，其後禁軍或降剩員，或升補，皆以備廂軍諸路力役之事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Xining, an edict ordered corridor troops inspected under the palace guard's five-division method; thereafter palace guards were either demoted to surplus rolls or promoted to fill gaps, all to supply corridor troops for corvée labor in the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Xining 3 (1070), an edict applied the palace guard's five-division system to corridor troops. Thereafter palace guards demoted to surplus rolls or promoted to fill gaps supplied corridor troops for provincial labor.

sentences.zh: 間詔募增，而京西轉運司所募多至三萬人；

translations.literal: From time to time edicts ordered additional recruitment, and the Jingxi transport office alone recruited as many as thirty thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Periodic edicts ordered further recruitment; the Jingxi transport office alone recruited up to thirty thousand;

sentences.zh: 陝西減額五千人，亦至三萬人。

translations.literal: Shaanxi, though its quota was reduced by five thousand, also reached thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: and Shaanxi, despite a five-thousand reduction in quota, also reached thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 河朔流民寓京東者如舊制招募教閱，以爲忠果二十指揮，分隸河北總管司，以除盜恤饑。

translations.literal: Migrants from Hebei lodged in Jingdong were recruited and drilled as before into twenty Loyal Fruit commands, distributed under the Hebei overall command, to suppress bandits and relieve famine.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei refugees in Jingdong were recruited and drilled into twenty Loyal Fruit commands under the Hebei overall command to suppress banditry and relieve famine.

sentences.zh: 而河北及熙河路修城壘，河北所募兵五千人，熙河亦三千人。

translations.literal: For repairing walls and ramparts in Hebei and the Xihe circuit, Hebei recruited five thousand soldiers and Xihe three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: For wall repair in Hebei and Xihe, Hebei recruited five thousand men and Xihe three thousand.

sentences.zh: 修京城，以廢馬監兵置廣固、保忠凡十指揮，亦五千人，湖南徭平，戎、瀘軍興，洮、河轉漕，又皆增置焉。

translations.literal: For repairing the capital, soldiers from abolished horse commissions were formed into Broad Works and Loyal Guard, ten commands in all, also five thousand men; when the Yao rebellion in Hunan was pacified, campaigns arose in Rong and Lu, and transport shifted on the Tao and He rivers, increases were made everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Capital repairs drew five thousand men from abolished horse commissions into ten Broad Works and Loyal Guard commands. Pacification of the Hunan Yao rebellion, campaigns in Rong and Lu, and Tao–He transport also brought further increases.

sentences.zh: 初，樞密院言：「京師役兵不足，歲取于諸路，而江、淮兵每饑凍，道斃相屬。

translations.literal: Initially the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: "Labor soldiers in the capital are insufficient; each year they are taken from the circuits, while Jiang and Huai troops often suffer hunger and freezing, dying along the road in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs first reported that capital labor troops were insufficient and drawn yearly from the circuits, while Jiang and Huai soldiers often starved and froze, dying in succession on the road.

sentences.zh: 略計歲所用外軍七千人，調發增給不貲。

translations.literal: Roughly calculated, seven thousand outside troops are used yearly; dispatch and added provisions are beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: About seven thousand outside troops were used yearly, with dispatch and extra provisions costing beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 請募東西八作司壯役指揮，諸司雜犯罪人情輕者並配隸，以次補雜役、效役，代諸路役兵，」從之。

translations.literal: We request recruiting Strong Labor commands in the East and West Eight Works Offices, assigning miscellaneous offenders from various offices whose circumstances are light, and in sequence filling miscellaneous and effective labor to replace labor troops from the circuits," and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: It requested recruiting Strong Labor commands in the East and West Eight Works Offices, assigning minor offenders from government offices, and filling labor rolls to replace troops from the circuits. The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 又言：「諸路廂軍名額猥多，自騎射至牢城，其名凡二百二十三。

translations.literal: It also reported: "Corridor-troop designations in the circuits are excessively numerous, from Cavalry Archers to Prison City, two hundred twenty-three names in all.
translations.idiomatic: It also noted that corridor-troop designations in the circuits were excessively numerous—from Cavalry Archers to Prison City, 223 names in all.

sentences.zh: 其間因事募人，團立新額，或因工作、榷酤、水陸運送、通道、山險、橋樑、郵傳、馬牧、提防、堰埭，若此者事在而名未可廢。

translations.literal: Among them, some recruited men for particular tasks and formed new quotas; some arose from labor, monopoly wine, water and land transport, passes, mountain hazards, bridges, postal relay, horse herding, embankments, and weirs—for such matters the tasks remain and the names cannot yet be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Some were raised for specific tasks; others served wine monopolies, transport, passes, mountain routes, bridges, postal relay, horse herding, embankments, and weirs—tasks that still required their designations.

sentences.zh: 及剩員直、牢城皆待有罪配隸之人；

translations.literal: Surplus rolls, duty rolls, and Prison City all await offenders assigned by punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Surplus rolls, duty rolls, and Prison City awaited convicted assignees;

sentences.zh: 壯城專治城隍，不給他役，別爲一軍；

translations.literal: Strong City specializes in city walls and moats, is given no other service, and forms a separate army;
translations.idiomatic: Strong City specialized in walls and moats, had no other duties, and formed a separate army;

translations.literal: while drilled corridor troops also have their own quotas.
translations.idiomatic: and drilled corridor troops had their own quotas.

sentences.zh: 請以諸路不教閱廂軍並爲一額，餘從省廢，其移並如禁軍法。」

translations.literal: We request merging all undrilled corridor troops in the circuits into one quota, abolishing the rest as the situation permits, with transfers and consolidations following palace-guard law.
translations.idiomatic: It proposed merging all undrilled corridor troops into one quota per circuit, abolishing the rest where possible, with transfers following palace-guard rules.

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 遂下諸路轉運司，以州大小高下爲序，始自某州爲第一指揮，差次至某州，凡爲若干指揮，每指揮毋過五百人。

translations.literal: Orders were then sent to the circuit transport offices to sequence prefectures by size and rank, beginning with a certain prefecture as the first command and in order to a certain prefecture, forming a set number of commands, each command not exceeding five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit transport offices were ordered to sequence prefectures by size, forming a set number of commands of no more than five hundred men each.

sentences.zh: 河北曰崇勝，河東曰雄猛，陝西曰保寧，京東曰奉化，京西曰勁武，淮南曰寧淮，兩浙曰崇節，江南曰效勇，荊湖曰宣節，福建曰保節，廣南曰清化，川四路曰克寧。

translations.literal: Hebei was called Victorious Respect, Hedong Fierce Bold, Shaanxi Secure Peace, Jingdong Submitting to Transformation, Jingxi Strong Martial, Huainan Pacifying Huai, Liangzhe Honored Integrity, Jiangnan Effective Valor, Jinghu Proclaiming Integrity, Fujian Guarding Integrity, Guangnan Pure Transformation, and the four Sichuan circuits Overcoming Peace.
translations.idiomatic: They were named Victorious Respect in Hebei, Fierce Bold in Hedong, Secure Peace in Shaanxi, Submitting to Transformation in Jingdong, Strong Martial in Jingxi, Pacifying Huai in Huainan, Honored Integrity in Liangzhe, Effective Valor in Jiangnan, Proclaiming Integrity in Jinghu, Guarding Integrity in Fujian, Pure Transformation in Guangnan, and Overcoming Peace in the four Sichuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔忻、代州諸砦，以禁軍代廂軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict ordered that in the stockades of Xin and Dai prefectures, palace guards replace corridor troops.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, an edict replaced corridor troops with palace guards in the stockades of Xin and Dai.

sentences.zh: 元豐四年，詔升南京、青、鄆、鄧、曹、濟、濮州有馬教閱廂軍，及真定府北砦勁勇、環州下蕃落未排定指揮，並爲禁軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, an edict promoted drilled corridor cavalry in Nanjing, Qing, Yan, Deng, Cao, Ji, and Pu prefectures, and the Strong Valor of the northern stockades of Zhending Prefecture and the unarranged frontier tribes commands below Huan prefecture, all to palace-guard status.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 4 (1081), an edict promoted drilled cavalry corridor troops in Nanjing, Qing, Yan, Deng, Cao, Ji, and Pu, plus Zhending's northern Strong Valor stockade and Huan's unarranged frontier-tribe commands, to palace-guard status.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，以西邊用兵，詔諸處役兵並罷，令諸路轉運司剗刷京東西、河東北、淮南廂軍，又令都水監刷河清及客軍共三萬餘人赴陝西團結。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, because of warfare on the western frontier, an edict halted labor troops everywhere and ordered circuit transport offices to muster corridor troops of Jingdong, Jingxi, Hedong, and Huainan; it also ordered the Directorate of Waterways to muster River Clear and guest troops, more than thirty thousand in all, to assemble in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 5, with war on the western frontier, an edict halted labor troops everywhere and ordered transport offices to muster corridor troops from Jingdong, Jingxi, Hedong, and Huainan. The Directorate of Waterways was to muster River Clear and guest troops—more than thirty thousand—to assemble in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔諸路教閱廂軍，於下禁軍內增入指揮名額，排連並同禁軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an edict ordered drilled corridor troops in the circuits to be added within lower palace-guard commands with command quotas, arranged in companies like palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, an edict incorporated drilled corridor troops into lower palace-guard commands with full company organization like palace guards.

sentences.zh: 於是，馬步排定有馬廂軍二十二指揮，無馬廂軍二百二十九指揮。

translations.literal: Thereupon, for horse and foot, twenty-two mounted corridor commands and two hundred twenty-nine unmounted corridor commands were arranged.
translations.idiomatic: Horse and foot were then arranged into twenty-two mounted and two hundred twenty-nine unmounted corridor commands.

sentences.zh: 元豐之末，總天下廂兵馬步指揮凡八百四十，其爲兵幾二十二萬七千六百二十七人，而府界及諸司或因事募兵之額不與焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanfeng, corridor horse-and-foot commands nationwide totaled eight hundred forty, with soldiers numbering nearly two hundred twenty-seven thousand six hundred twenty-seven, not counting the capital district and various offices' ad hoc recruitment quotas.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Yuanfeng, corridor commands nationwide totaled 840, with about 227,627 soldiers, not counting the capital district or ad hoc recruitment by government offices.

sentences.zh: 哲宗元祐二年，太師文彥博言：「廂軍舊隸樞密院，新制改隸兵部，且本兵之府豈可無籍？」

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou under Emperor Zhezong, Grand Mentor Wen Yanbo said: "Corridor troops were formerly subordinate to the Bureau of Military Affairs; the new system changed them to the Ministry of War—yet how can the headquarters of the army be without registers?
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 2 (1087), Grand Mentor Wen Yanbo said: "Corridor troops formerly reported to the Bureau of Military Affairs; the new system moved them to the Ministry of War. How can the army's headquarters lack registers?

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs also spoke on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs made the same point.

sentences.zh: 乃詔本部自今進冊，以其副上樞密院。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered the ministry henceforth to submit registers, sending a copy to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ministry to submit registers hereafter, with copies to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔京西路廂軍以三萬五百人爲額，又詔天下州郡以地理置壯城兵。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict fixed Jingxi corridor troops at a quota of thirty thousand five hundred men; another edict ordered all prefectures and commanderies under Heaven to establish Strong City troops according to geography.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, Jingxi corridor troops were fixed at 30,500. Another edict ordered prefectures nationwide to establish Strong City troops according to local geography.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，詔罪人應配五百里以上，皆配陝西、河東充廂軍，諸路經略司各二千人止。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, an edict ordered that offenders to be assigned five hundred li or more were all assigned to Shaanxi and Hedong as corridor troops, each circuit frontier command limited to two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 1 (1098), offenders assigned exile of five hundred li or more were sent to Shaanxi and Hedong as corridor troops, each frontier command limited to two thousand.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔撥陝西保甯指揮入諸路廂軍額。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict transferred Shaanxi Secure Peace commands into the corridor-troop quotas of the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, Shaanxi Secure Peace commands were transferred into circuit corridor-troop quotas.

sentences.zh: 崇寧四年，詔諸路廂軍不以等樣選少壯人招刺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongning, an edict ordered corridor troops in the circuits, regardless of grade, to select young and strong men for recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 4 (1105), an edict ordered all corridor commands to recruit young and strong men regardless of grade.

sentences.zh: 又詔：廂軍工匠除上京修造外，其餘路所差，並放還休息之。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered: apart from craftsmen sent to the capital for construction, those dispatched by other circuits were all released to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict released corridor craftsmen assigned outside the capital for construction, sending them home to rest.

sentences.zh: 政和五年，廣固四指揮各增五百人，以備京城之役。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenghe, each of the four Broad Works commands was increased by five hundred men to prepare for capital labor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 5 (1115), each of the four Broad Works commands added five hundred men for capital labor.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，增置通濟兵士二千人，備御前牽挽綱運。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, two thousand Universal Relief soldiers were added to prepare for imperial towing of canal transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 6, two thousand Universal Relief soldiers were added for imperial canal towing duty.

sentences.zh: 於是工役日興，增募益廣矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon public works daily flourished, and recruitment grew ever broader.
translations.idiomatic: Public works expanded daily, and recruitment grew ever broader.

sentences.zh: 建炎而後，兵制靡定，逮乾道中，四川廂軍二萬九百七十二人，禁軍二萬七千九百九十二人。

translations.literal: After Jianyan, the military system was unsettled; by the Qiandao era, Sichuan corridor troops numbered twenty thousand nine hundred seventy-two, palace guards twenty-seven thousand nine hundred ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianyan, military organization was unstable. By the Qiandao era, Sichuan had 20,972 corridor troops and 27,992 palace guards.

sentences.zh: 厥後廢置損益，隨時不同，摭其可考者以附見焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter abolitions, establishments, increases, and decreases differed with the times; what can be verified is gathered here for reference.
translations.idiomatic: Later abolitions and changes varied with the times; what can be verified is recorded here for reference.

sentences.zh: 其將校則有馬步軍都指揮使，有副都指揮使、都虞候。

translations.literal: Their officers included horse-and-foot army commanders-in-chief, with deputy commanders-in-chief and chief adjutants.
translations.idiomatic: Their officers included horse-and-foot commanders-in-chief, deputy commanders-in-chief, and chief adjutants.

sentences.zh: 馬軍有都指揮使、副都指揮使、都虞候，步軍亦如之。

translations.literal: The cavalry had commanders-in-chief, deputy commanders-in-chief, and chief adjutants; the infantry likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry had commanders-in-chief, deputies, and chief adjutants; infantry had the same.

sentences.zh: 馬步軍諸指揮有指揮使、副指揮使。

translations.literal: Each horse-and-foot command had a commander and deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Each horse-and-foot command had a commander and deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 每都有軍使、副兵馬使、都頭、副都頭、十將、將虞候、承局、押官。

translations.literal: Each company had a troop commissioner, deputy horse-and-foot commissioner, company chief, deputy company chief, centurion, adjutant, clerk, and escort officer.
translations.idiomatic: Each company had a troop commissioner, deputy horse-and-foot commissioner, company chief, deputy company chief, centurion, adjutant, clerk, and escort officer.

sentences.zh: 凡諸州騎兵、步兵、禁廂兵之類，敘列如左。

translations.literal: All types such as cavalry, infantry, and imperial corridor troops in the various prefectures are set forth below.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry, infantry, imperial corridor troops, and related types in the prefectures are listed below.

sentences.zh: 其不同者，分爲建隆以來及熙寧以後之制雲。

translations.literal: Where they differ, they are divided into the institutions since Jianlong and since Xining, as follows.
translations.idiomatic: Where arrangements differ, they are divided into institutions from the Jianlong era onward and from the Xining era onward, as set out below.

translations.literal: Institutions since Jianlong
translations.idiomatic: Institutions since Jianlong

sentences.zh: 騎射京東路：南京、青、兗、鄆、曹、徐、齊、濰、淮陽。

translations.literal: Cavalry Archers, Jingdong Circuit: Nanjing, Qing, Yan, Yun, Cao, Xu, Qi, Wei, and Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry Archers, Jingdong Circuit: Nanjing, Qing, Yan, Yun, Cao, Xu, Qi, Wei, and Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 京西路：西京、河陽、陳、許、鄭、潁、滑。

translations.literal: Jingxi Circuit: Xijing, Heyang, Chen, Xu, Zheng, Ying, and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxi Circuit: Xijing, Heyang, Chen, Xu, Zheng, Ying, and Hua.

sentences.zh: 河北路：北京、真定、滄、澶、相、恩、冀。

translations.literal: Hebei Circuit: Bejing, Zhending, Cang, Chan, Xiang, En, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei Circuit: Bejing, Zhending, Cang, Chan, Xiang, En, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 陝西路：永興、鳳翔、河中、陝、華、秦、涇、鄜。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Circuit: Yongxing, Fengxiang, Hezhong, Shan, Hua, Qin, Jing, and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Circuit: Yongxing, Fengxiang, Hezhong, Shan, Hua, Qin, Jing, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 荊湖路：江陵、潭、鄂、岳、復、安、澧、鼎、永、道、郴、邵、桂陽。

translations.literal: Jinghu Circuit: Jiangling, Tan, E, Yue, Fu, An, Li, Ding, Yong, Dao, Chen, Shao, and Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghu Circuit: Jiangling, Tan, E, Yue, Fu, An, Li, Ding, Yong, Dao, Chen, Shao, and Guiyang.

translations.literal: Among them, Qing and Huaiyang were classified as drilled.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, Qing and Huaiyang were drilled units.

sentences.zh: 威邊京東路：南京、青、鄆、密、徐、曹、齊、濮、濟、淄、登、萊、沂、單。

translations.literal: Border Guard, Jingdong Circuit: Nanjing, Qing, Yun, Mi, Xu, Cao, Qi, Pu, Ji, Zi, Deng, Lai, Yi, and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Border Guard, Jingdong Circuit: Nanjing, Qing, Yun, Mi, Xu, Cao, Qi, Pu, Ji, Zi, Deng, Lai, Yi, and Shan.
